title: Bah Sz En

page_data.en:

11/5/16

Shanghai Municipal Council.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH.)

May 6th 1916.

Sir,
It is reported that a rebel leader named Bah Sz
En白士安 paid eighty of his followers $2.00 each
yesterday afternoon in the western part of Frenchtown
and told them to get ready to attack Chapel last night
adding that he had made arrangements to have the
soldiers in Chapel join them. The men took the money
but failed to muster.
It is reported that General Chang Hsun has placed
5000 soldiers at the disposal of the ex-Governor of
Chekiang to enable him to retake that province.
The ex-Governor may advance on Chekiang through Anhwei.
About 1 a.m. 5th instant a number of Japanese and
others carrying small parcels boarded a launch, the
property of Dr. Wong, Red Cross Hospital, on Soochow
Creek and demanded to be taken to the river.
The loudah pretended that the engines had gone out of
order whereupon the party returned and moored the boat
at Peking Road jetty. The loudah has been detained
by the River Police.
On the morning of April 5th about twenty persons
went to Woosung on a steam launch which went alongside
the Chinese gunboat Tsa De 策電 lying in the river there.
Six of the party who were armed with pistols went
on board the gunboat with the intention of causing the
crew to turn over to the rebels, but they were all
arrested and detained. The remainder of the band
escaped on the launch which returned to Shanghai.
Two of the men arrested are believed to be Japanese
although they do not claim that nationality.
A number of the persons who escaped had also the
appearance of being Japanese.
Over one hundred Japanese who have come to Shanghai
in connection with the projected insurrections of the
rebels are leaving to-day for Japan by the N.Y.K. steamer.
They have each received the sum of twenty five yen.
The rebels have very little money at the present moment.
Sun Yat Sen is reported as having arrived in
Shanghai on his way to Hangchow.
Your Obedient Servant,
（签名）
Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

（左侧手写批注：）
Entered on
Mr. J. Mac...
K.P.

刑事侦缉处
317
16/5/11

上海工部局。

（印：上海工部局警务处）
警务处，
（侦探股。）

1916年5月6日。

先生：

据报，一名名为白士安（Bah Sz En）的叛乱头目昨日下午在法租界西部向其八十名追随者每人支付2.00美元，并命令他们准备好于昨晚袭击小教堂（Chapel），还称他已安排让小教堂内的士兵加入他们。这些人收下了钱，但未能集结。

据报，张勋将军已将5000名士兵交由浙江前督军支配，以便其夺回该省。该前督军可能会经由安徽进军浙江。

本月5日凌晨1时许，多名日本人及其他携带小包裹的人士登上停泊在苏州河上的红十字医院黄医生（Dr. Wong）所属的一艘汽艇，并要求将其载往江面。船夫佯称引擎发生故障，随后该伙人返回，并将船停靠在北京路码头。该船夫已被水上警察拘留。

4月5日上午，约二十人乘坐一艘汽艇前往吴淞，该汽艇靠上了停泊在该处江面上的中国炮舰“策电”号。该伙人中持有手枪的六人登上炮舰，意图迫使船员倒戈加入叛军，但他们全部被捕并被拘留。其余匪徒乘原汽艇逃回上海。

被捕人员中有两人虽未声称拥有日本国籍，但据信为日本人。

逃脱的人员中也有多人看似日本人。

一百多名因参与叛军策划的起义而来到上海的日本人，今日将乘坐日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）的轮船离开前往日本。他们每人收到了二十五日元。

目前叛军资金非常匮乏。

据报，孙中山在前往杭州的途中抵达上海。

您顺从的仆人，

（签名）
总探长。

警务处处长。

（左侧手写批注：）
录入于
J. Mac... 先生
K.P.

29/5/16

Shanghai Municipal Council.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH.)

May 25th 1913.

Sir,
The names of the six Japanese who were arrested at Woosung when attempting to board the Chinese gunboat Cha Do 肇和 on May 5th, handed over to the Japanese Consul and subsequently sent to Japan on May 20 per S.S. Yamashiro Maru, are:-
Yosaku Oyama.
Shimakichi Takeuchi.
Tsunojiro Yoshimura.
Yoneji Ito.
Yotaro Suzuki.
Masana Ouchi.

They stated that they were brought from Japan by another Japanese whose name is Tomeji Shinozawa and were led to believe that they would go on board peaceably and be employed as gunners on a man-of-war and were surprised that they met with resistance when they mounted the gangway of the vessel at Woosung.

Tomeji Shinozawa appears to have been responsible for still another person who furnished the money but who remained in the background. His name is said to be Matsuo and he deals direct with the revolutionary leaders and handles their money. He stays in the Towa Hotel and entertains very lavishly.

Your obedient servant,

（签名）

Chief Detective Inspector.

（批：AM） （签名）
Captain Superintendent of Police.

（批：... May 26.）

上海工部局。

（印：上海工部局警务处）
警务处，
（侦探股。）

1913年5月25日。

先生：

5月5日在吴淞试图登上中国炮舰“肇和”号（Cha Do）时被捕的六名日本人的姓名如下，他们已被移交给日本领事，并于5月20日乘坐“山城丸”号（S.S. Yamashiro Maru）轮船被遣送回国：

大山与作（Yosaku Oyama）。
竹内岛吉（Shimakichi Takeuchi）。
吉村津之次郎（Tsunojiro Yoshimura）。
伊藤米次（Yoneji Ito）。
铃木洋太郎（Yotaro Suzuki）。
大内正名（Masana Ouchi）。

他们称，是另一名名为篠泽留次（Tomeji Shinozawa）的日本人将他们从日本带来，并让他们相信他们将和平登船，受雇为一艘军舰上的炮手；因此，当他们在吴淞登上该船舷梯时遭遇抵抗，感到十分惊讶。

篠泽留次似乎还对另一人负责，此人提供了资金但躲在幕后。据说此人名叫松尾（Matsuo），他与革命领袖直接联系并掌管他们的资金。他住在东亚酒店（Towa Hotel），招待极为铺张。

您顺从的仆人，

（签名）

总探长。

（批：AM） （签名）
警务处处长。

（批：... 5月26日。）
